draft.title: Buffers
card: A buffer is a solution that resists a change in pH when a small amount of acid or base is added. It holds a weak acid and its conjugate base together in the same solution.
reacts with any added base (OH⁻). This removes the extra base and keeps the pH close to where it was.
reacts with any added acid (H⁺). This removes the extra acid and keeps the pH close to where it was.

An example is ethanoic acid with sodium ethanoate. Blood is also buffered, mainly by carbonic acid and hydrogencarbonate ions, so its pH stays in a narrow range. A buffer has a limit: a large amount of acid or base can use up one of the two partners and the pH then changes.
draft.remember: A buffer holds a weak acid and its conjugate base, so it can absorb small amounts of added base or acid.

a.q: Why can a mixture of ethanoic acid and sodium ethanoate act as a buffer?
opts: It holds a weak acid and its conjugate base together
It holds a strong acid and a strong base together
It contains a lot of water, which dilutes added acid
It contains a salt that blocks any added acid or base
a.why: Ethanoic acid reacts with added base and ethanoate ions react with added acid, so the pH changes little. A strong acid and a strong base would neutralise each other, not form a buffer.
a.clue: Which pair can deal with both added acid and added base?

b.q: A buffer contains the weak acid HA and its conjugate base A⁻. A small amount of hydrochloric acid is added. What happens?
opts: A⁻ reacts with the added H⁺ and the pH changes only slightly
HA reacts with the added H⁺ and the pH changes only slightly
The added H⁺ stays free and the pH falls sharply
A⁻ reacts with the added H⁺ and the pH is fixed exactly
b.why: The conjugate base A⁻ removes added H⁺ by forming HA, so the pH changes only slightly. HA is the partner that reacts with added base, not acid. The pH is resisted, not held exactly fixed.
b.clue: Which partner in the buffer can accept H⁺?

a.best: It holds a weak acid and its conjugate base together

b.best: A⁻ reacts with the added H⁺ and the pH changes only slightly
